note: Cross-border payments APIs, London. GV led the GBP 20M ($25M) Series D in March 2017 as a new investor, its first fintech investment in Europe (TechCrunch, 'London-based'); GV was an existing backer in the $80M Series E of January 2020 (Crunchbase News). Visa bought it in 2021 (Reuters headline, 'at 700 million pounds valuation'; the firm's own exit line 'Acquired by Visa, 2021').

Third-party cyber risk exchange, Denver. Google Ventures is named among the investors when the company announced $20M in April 2017 ($29M raised in total; CyberScoop), but no source names that round or says whether GV was already in the $9M of 2016, and the next round is a named Series C ($30M, December 2018, Scale Venture Partners leading, GV an existing investor). Stage undetermined; no entry date. ProcessUnity and its investors acquired CyberGRX in July 2023 (SiliconANGLE).

Social Ethereum block explorer founded by Eric Feng (ex-Hulu CTO). Decrypt (July 2023) reports $18.5M raised in total with GV among the investors and names no round, so the stage is undetermined. cymbal.xyz serves only a logo splash page (read 2026-09-28) and nothing has been reported since mid-2023: defunct, aligned with First Round's row (status and city), though the firm still lists it.

funding_rounds.round: total raised to date, no round named

note: Residential geothermal heating and cooling, spun out of X. GV led the $40M Series C of September 2024; the release is datelined Arlington, Virginia and gives it as the headquarters (the move is in the Washington Business Journal's headline). No valuation disclosed and no later priced round found.

CryptoKitties, NBA Top Shot and Flow, Vancouver. GV joined the $15M round of November 2018 led by Venrock (the company's release, datelined Vancouver; $27.85M raised in total, after the $12M Series A of March 2018 that a16z and USV led, per their rows); no source names the November round, so the stage is undetermined with the entry date kept. The last priced mark is the $250M round led by Coatue at $7.6B, GV participating (CoinDesk, 2021-09-22), re-sourced from the unicorn list and stale; aligned with the Coatue and USV rows. Accel's 'Dapper' row is a different company (Yahoo's 2010 purchase).

Anti-malware for websites and ad networks, Sunnyvale (Wikipedia). Google Ventures invested in February 2011, amount undisclosed and no round named, after $4M from Benhamou Global Ventures, Floodgate, Radar Partners and others (TechCrunch): stage undetermined. Twitter acquired it in January 2012 (Wikipedia; the firm's exit line).

Private-company intelligence platform. The launch release (Palo Alto, 2014-02-05) names a seed round backed by Google Ventures; TechCrunch later put it at $1.78M. The $5M of July 2015 (Goldman Sachs and Green Visor) was structured as a seed, 'not a Series A' (TechCrunch, 'Palo Alto-based'), so it does not graduate the row by name; DataFox was last valued at $33M in January 2017 and had raised just under $19M when Oracle bought it in October 2018 (TechCrunch). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

funding_rounds.round: Seed (structured as seed, not a Series A)
funding_rounds.lead: Goldman Sachs and Green Visor Capital

note: Analytics engineering (dbt), Philadelphia. GV came in as a new investor in the $222M Series D of February 2022, led by Altimeter at a $4.2B valuation (the company's release, datelined Philadelphia). Merged into Fivetran in an all-stock deal completed in 2026 (the firm's own exit line 'Acquired by Fivetran, 2026'); acquired, aligned with the a16z, Coatue and Sequoia rows.

Inner-ear gene therapies, Boston (the S-1's principal executive offices, 1325 Boylston Street). The draft S-1's related-person table lists GV 2016, L.P. buying 5,000,000 shares of Series A preferred ($5.0M) in the Series A closings of January and May 2017, beside Third Rock and S.R. One. The Form D band had read the 2020 Series D filing as a Growth entry; disputed with the filing. Regeneron acquired the company in 2023 (status pre-filled).

Haystack, the open-source LLM application framework, Berlin. GV led the $14M Series A, the company's first funding round after years bootstrapped (TechCrunch, April 2022; the firm's own post calls it GV's first investment in Germany); the round closed in 2021, and the firm's /ai list dates GV's first investment December 2021, used as the entry date. Balderton led the $30M round of August 2023 with GV following (TechCrunch). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the name with raises, 2025 and 2026): no later round and no priced mark at or above $1B; aligned with Balderton's row.

Activation-lethality cancer medicines, Cambridge MA (One Kendall Square). The company launched in May 2024 with a $67M Series A led by GV, with Nextech, Polaris Innovation Fund and Alexandria (the company's release). Endpoints already called it GV-backed in September 2023 (headline), so the Series A was likely committed before the launch; the entry date is the release's.

Neurodegeneration drugs, South San Francisco (the S-1's principal executive offices). The Series A-1 investors' rights agreement of 8 May 2015 lists Google Ventures 2015, L.P. among the investors after the additional closings of 22 May and 22 July 2015 (the S-1 exhibit), so GV entered at the Series A; the Form D band had read the 2024 private placement, years after the 2017 IPO, as the entry. Market cap $3.35B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com) replaces the SEC float.

Metal 3D printing, Burlington MA (Wikipedia). GV led the $45M Series C announced in February 2017 (Wikipedia), after a Series A from NEA, Kleiner Perkins and Lux and further 2016 money; the firm's own post says 'I first invested in the company in late 2016'. Same stage as the Form D band, which had dated the entry to the 2019 filing; re-sourced and re-dated. Nano Dimension bought it in 2025 and it filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025 (Wikipedia): acquired (pre-filled), aligned with Lux.

The free online graphing calculator (desmos.com), San Francisco. The pre-filled Greece and 'defunct' (dissolved 1993) come from a Wikidata join on the one-word name, disputed. Google Ventures invested in September 2012, terms undisclosed, bringing total funding past $1M after $800K from Kapor, Learn Capital and Kindler; the money was meant to open a Series A that Desmos then held off raising (TechCrunch), so no round name holds: stage undetermined. Amplify acquired the Desmos curriculum and teacher.desmos.com in May 2022 and the calculator was spun off as Desmos Studio PBC (Wikipedia): acquired, with Desmos Studio the successor for the calculator.

Deep-learning training platform, San Francisco. The firm's own post lists its early AI infrastructure investments as 'Determined AI (Series A, 2018; acquired by HPE)' and says GV led the Series A; the /ai list dates GV's first investment November 2018 (entry date, decisions D7) and a re-investment April 2020. Hewlett Packard Enterprise acquired it in 2021 (the firm's exit line).

Medicare Advantage plan and medical group, Waltham MA. The company's own page names GV among the new investors in its $48M Series F (November 2025) and $317M Series F-Prime (January 2026), both led by The Space Between and Centricus: a Series F entry, Growth; the entry date is the Series F's month (GV may have come in at the F-Prime). No valuation was published for either; the last published mark is the $1.15B Series D of October 2021 at $12.6B (MedCity News), re-sourced from the unicorn list, stale, and aligned with ICONIQ Growth's row. Press figures for the 2026 rounds disagree and the reported talks at $25B are not a priced event.

AI business communications, formerly Firespotter Labs and Switch; Dialpad, Inc. gives 2700 Camino Ramon, San Ramon as its address (its terms). GV's entry was Firespotter's 'initial $3 million round of funding from Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, May 2011); a16z then led the $15M Series B of July 2012 with Google Ventures an existing and its earliest investor (the company's release), so the 2011 round is the Series A by position (model, medium). The Form D band had read the 2020 filing as a Growth entry; disputed. Last priced mark: the $170M Series F led by ICONIQ at $2.2B, GV participating (the company's release, 2021-12-16), stale; aligned with the a16z, Felicis and ICONIQ rows.

Automated savings app, San Francisco ('San Francisco-based', TechCrunch 2016). The pre-filled Japan and 'defunct' come from a Wikidata join on the one-word name, disputed. Google Ventures was in the $2.5M seed led by Baseline Ventures (TechCrunch, December 2014); an $11.3M Series A followed about a year before the $22.5M Series B led by Ribbit Capital (TechCrunch, June 2016): graduated. Oportun completed its acquisition on 22 December 2021 for about $211.1M (GlobeNewswire); aligned with the General Catalyst and Ribbit rows.

Automated accounting for small businesses (Jeff Seibert). Benchmark led the $10.5M Series A of 2019 with no GV; GV's Jessica Verrilli led the $22M Series B (TechCrunch, April 2020). SoftBank's Vision Fund led the $65M Series C at $565M with GV following (TechCrunch, March 2022). Remote-first; city aligned with 20VC's row.

Glasses-free mixed-reality optics and heads-up displays for vehicles and defence, Helsinki. After a $2.7M pre-seed led by FOV Ventures and Maki.vc (June 2024), GV led the EUR 10M seed (the company's release, Helsinki, 24 September 2024). FORVIA HELLA made an undisclosed strategic investment in September 2026 (the company's news page), no round named or amount given. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Community health teams embedded in primary care for Medicaid patients (Illinois, Michigan, Ohio and New York markets on its careers page). Endpoints' headline reports the GV-backed company raising $52M (November 2024), matching the $52.4M sold on its 2024 Form D, where the chief executive files from Chicago and the issuer address is a director's in Glencoe, Illinois. No valuation disclosed.

Enterprise mobile 'dual persona' platform, formerly Enterproid, New York. Google Ventures joined the $11M Series A led by Comcast Ventures, with Qualcomm Ventures (TechCrunch, October 2011). Google bought Divide in May 2014 (CNBC and Forbes headlines; the firm's exit line).

Video visits with physicians, San Francisco (its Form Ds, 275 Battery Street). Google Ventures was in the $3M seed with Venrock, Andreessen Horowitz, Lerer and Shasta at launch (TechCrunch, December 2013); Venrock and Shasta led the $21M Series A of August 2014 (TechCrunch): graduated. Merged with Grand Rounds in May 2021 and rebranded Included Health (PR Newswire and Healthcare Dive headlines): acquired, aligned with the a16z row.

E-signature and agreement software, San Francisco (Wikipedia). The capitalization table in the draft S-1's credit-agreement exhibit (30 April 2015) shows Google Ventures holding 1,751,781 Series D and 102,338 Series E preferred, plus small Series B and common positions; TechCrunch's headline of August 2012 has Google Ventures joining the round that grew to $55.7M. Entry at the Series D: Growth. Market cap $12.52B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com) replaces the SEC float; aligned with the Accel, Bain Capital Ventures and Insight rows.
Endpoint secure web gateway, Mountain View (its 2023 Form D). The firm's own post of March 2023 says GV led the $16M Series A, matching the pre-filled stage. No later round or valuation found.

Universal secrets manager for developers (YC W19). The pre-filled Austria is a Wikidata join on the one-word name, disputed: Y Combinator's directory lists it active in Austin, TX (read 2026-09-28; remote-first), aligned with the YC row over Sequoia's San Francisco. GV led the $6.5M round of March 2021 (the firm's own post; Forbes headline); no source names it, but it falls between the $2.3M seed of October 2020 (Sequoia's row) and the $20M Series A that CRV led in April 2022 with GV following (TechCrunch): a second seed round (model, medium), graduated by the named Series A. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the name with raises, 2025): no later round, no $1B mark.

note: AI-generated technical documentation for codebases (driver.ai), Austin (Driver AI, Inc.'s Form D of October 2024, $8.27M sold). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on 'Driver AI' raises): no later round, no $1B mark. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

AI-native ERP, New York (7 World Trade Center, its site). Lightspeed and Khosla led the $90M Series A of 2 October 2025 with GV, Contrary and Vesey (the company's announcement); the firm's /ai list dates GV's first investment October 2025, so GV was not in the earlier seed. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the name with raises and valuation): no later round; the only figure seen is a vendor's $415M (Rule A, not a mark). Aligned with Lightspeed's row.

note: Two-factor authentication, Ann Arbor MI (TechCrunch). Google Ventures led the $5M Series A of February 2012 with True Ventures and Resonant (TechCrunch 2012; the 2014 piece names it 'a $5 million Series A round led by Google Ventures'); Benchmark led the $12M Series B of 2014. Cisco bought Duo for $2.35B in 2018 (the firm's exit line): acquired, aligned with the Benchmark and Redpoint rows.

AI-designed AAV capsids for gene therapy, Watertown MA (343 Arsenal Street, its site). GV joined the $100M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in May 2021 (the release on SynBioBeta; the firm's /ai list dates GV's investment April 2021); earlier operations ran on a seed from Polaris, CRV and KdT. Aligned with the a16z and Lux rows.

Multi-carrier shipping API (legal name Simpler Postage, Inc.). Its $850K seed of June 2013 (YC, SV Angel and others) did not include Google Ventures (TechCrunch); GV listed it from 2014, and only vendor profiles tie GV to a February 2014 seed (Rule A: not citable), so the stage is undetermined. A July 2026 auction notice for 2,456,673 pledged common shares says the 2021 and 2022 rounds valued it at about $1.52B post-money and that it remains privately held with over $100M of 2025 revenue; no auction price is published, so the last primary stands, stale. City: Simpler Postage's March 2025 Form D files from Lehi, Utah (fresher than the San Francisco on the General Catalyst and YC rows).

CRISPR genome-editing medicines, Cambridge MA (the S-1's principal executive offices, 300 Third Street). The amended investors' rights agreement of 4 August 2015, signed with the Series B stock purchase agreement, adds Google Ventures 2014, L.P. to the Series A-1 and A-2 holders (Flagship, Polaris, Third Rock, Partners); the A-2 was a tranche of the 2013 Series A commitments, so GV entered at the Series B (the S-1 exhibit). Market cap $385.49M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com) replaces the SEC float; band unchanged.

Cloud content collaboration and governance, Mountain View (Wikipedia). Google Ventures led the $16M Series C of July 2012 with existing investors Kleiner Perkins and Polaris; Karim Faris joined the board (Growth Business). In February 2025 GI Partners and TA Associates became majority shareholders (Wikipedia; the firm's exit line 'GI Partners and TA Associates, 2025'): a private-equity buyout, acquired.

Wearable cardioverter-defibrillator patch (Jewel), San Francisco (its Form Ds, 2014 to 2016). The $145.6M Series C of March 2020 (Business Wire and FinSMEs headlines) is the last priced round found, valuation undisclosed; FDA approval in May 2025 (Fierce Biotech headline), operating. The pre-filled stage (Form D band) is left as it stands: no source names the 2014 round.

Mobius, a mobile app for capturing and sharing moments in virtual reality. Its only Form D (Emergent VR, Inc., San Jose, first sale January 2015) is a $2M convertible-note offering; Road to VR reported $2.2M raised from Accel, Google Ventures and Rothenberg Ventures in October 2015, the company's first money and no round named: Seed by instrument and size (model, medium). The firm's exit line reads 'Acquired by River Studios, 2018'. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Precision gene therapy for Dravet syndrome (ETX101), South San Francisco. The firm's own post of July 2020: David Schenkein and Brendan Bulik-Sullivan 'chose to lead Encoded's Series D funding', and the firm lists it from 2020; Menlo had entered at the 2019 Series C. The company raised a $275M Series F in September 2026 (Business Wire headline, no valuation found). Aligned with Menlo's row.

Video-based English learning, Lexington MA (its only Form D, 2009; 'based in Massachusetts', TechCrunch 2010); the site is live (copyright 2026). Google Ventures led a seed round of convertible debt in October 2009 ($1.38M), which converted into a $2.1M Series A in December 2009 (TechCrunch: 'the current series A financing', backed by Google Ventures and Atlas Venture): the named later round graduates the row, two months after the seed. NTT Investment Partners added $1M in November 2010 (TechCrunch). The pre-filled Seed (Form D band) is re-sourced and re-dated to the seed itself.

Bispecific-antibody protein degraders, San Mateo (the company's releases). GV was in the $50M Series A co-led by Mubadala Capital and Polaris Partners (the company's release, 22 March 2023: 'with participation from Vivo Capital and GV'); the $23M extension of July 2023 came from Digitalis, Taiho and Codon; GV and JJDC co-led the $107M Series B of January 2026 with GV an existing investor (the company's release). The firm lists it only from 2026, after the Series B.

Cloud platform for genomic and biomedical data, Mountain View (Wikipedia; the release). Google Ventures and TPG Biotech led the company's $15M 'second-round funding' of 12 October 2011, with First Round, SoftTech, K9 and Felicis following (the release on Fierce Biotech); the company's own blog calls those four previous investors and Google Ventures and TPG new ones. Felicis, already in before October 2011, labels its own entry Series A on its listing (after the $1.55M First Round, K9 and SoftTech put in from 2009, Wikipedia), and the $15M of January 2014 was a Series C (Wikipedia), so GV's entry is the Series B by position: Growth (model, medium). The pre-filled entry date (the 2014 Form D) is replaced. Blackstone Growth led $200M in 2022 (Business Wire headline), valuation undisclosed.

Satellite manufacturer, Sofia (the company's releases). After a $10M Series A led by CEECAT Capital in May 2023 that does not name GV, Google Ventures joined the $104M round of 30 October 2025 with Riot Ventures, Lux and the EIC Fund (the company's release; the firm lists it from 2025): an unnamed round after the Series A, Growth (model, medium). GV is also in the $205M round of September 2026 led by Riot Ventures and Atreides. Valuation check 2026-09-28: the company's CMO told The Recursive the valuation has 'blown past $1B' but will not disclose the figure (BTA and Intellinews report the same); with no figure the row reads below $1B under Rule A (the MatX precedent), flagged for the web pass.

Marketplace matching B2B salespeople with 'emissaries' who know their target accounts, founded by ex-Googler David Hammer, New York (its Form Ds). At its November 2016 launch it announced a $10M Series A led by Canaan Partners and G20 Ventures, 'after a $2 million seed round with participation from GV' and The New York Times (Business Insider): Seed, graduated. The entry date is the year of that report; the seed preceded the launch. Emissary, Inc. kept raising small rounds through July 2024 (Form D, $4.5M sold), but emissary.io is now parked for sale (read 2026-09-28) and no later news was found: defunct; emissary.ai is an unrelated recruiting company.

AI shopping and fashion discovery (daydream.ing), founded by Julie Bornstein; headquarters in Kirkland, WA (425 Business; the seed release is datelined New York). GV joined the $50M seed co-led by Forerunner and Index with True Ventures (the company's release, 20 June 2024; TechCrunch). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the name with Julie Bornstein and raises): no later round and no $1B mark; TechCrunch's June 2025 launch piece still cites only the seed. The First Round row (daydream Labs, an AI SEO agency in San Francisco) and the 8VC row (DayDream, dental AI) are different companies. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Technographics and sales-prospecting data (which software a website runs). A few months after an April 2014 pitch, Mark Cuban 'joined IDG Ventures and Google Ventures in a $2 million seed-round investment' (Business Insider, January 2015); TechCrunch dates the $2M seed to 2014. No later round found. Zoom Information, Inc. (the legacy ZoomInfo, a Great Hill Partners company that DiscoverOrg bought in 2019) acquired it in 2018; its adviser Cascadia Capital gives it as 'headquartered in San Mateo, California' (the firm's exit line: 'Acquired by ZoomInfo, 2018'). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Net Promoter customer-feedback surveys, founded in 2013 by Caleb Elston with engineers from Yobongo and Mosaic. Its first announced funding, amount undisclosed, came from Google Ventures, Shasta Ventures, SV Angel, Designer Fund, Fuel Capital, Relay Ventures and angels a year after launch (TechCrunch, October 2014); no round is named, and the syndicate reads as a seed (model, medium). Qualtrics acquired it on 12 April 2018 (the release; the firm's exit line). City not placed: the release's dateline (Salt Lake City and Seattle) is Qualtrics', and neither TechCrunch's launch pieces nor EDGAR give an address; an M&A database's Palo Alto could not be read. Graduation left for the graduation pass.
